Voice input needs a speech recognition service (e.g. Google app or Speech Services by Google). None is installed.
Speech recognition needs a connection (or an offline language pack).

Saqr uses the microphone only while you hold a dictation open, to turn your speech into text in the message box. Audio goes to your phone’s speech recognition service; Saqr doesn’t record or upload it.
Allow the microphone for Saqr Code in the app settings to use voice input.
Saqr keeps working when you leave the app or lock the screen. Some phones still stop background apps to save battery.

Infinix/Tecno (XOS), Xiaomi (MIUI/HyperOS), Huawei, Oppo, Vivo and Samsung are known to do this. Allow Saqr to run without battery restrictions (and, on Infinix/Xiaomi, turn on “Auto-start” in the app settings).
Tasks continue with a notification when you leave the app or the screen locks
Stop the phone from killing long tasks
Send the message as soon as you stop speaking
Tip: long-press the mic to switch between Arabic and English.
Keeps listening while a project is open. In wake mode, say “Ya Saqr” then your command and it sends itself. Stop any time from the notification or the mic button.
No network, no drama: cloud features pause with one clear message — local commands, the terminal, memory, local commits and the on-device build (from a cached environment) keep working.
Desert active — cloud features are paused; everything local keeps working.
Network available — cloud features are on.
Desert mode: the agent, web tools, remote MCP and push/pull are paused until the network returns. Files, terminal, local commits and the cached build environment still work.

Desert mode is active (no network): sending a command needs a connection. Everything local — files, terminal, memory, local commits, the cached build environment — still works, and your text stays here unsent.
A .saqrpack installs a project template, ready Arabic commands, AGENTS.md rules and preferred tools in one tap. Installed packs appear as templates on the home screen.
Invalid pack — check the content and try again
Flask pack installed — its template is on the home screen
Arabic packs from the community\'s public repository (CTO-DRS/saqr-gallery) — one tap installs a template with its commands. Contribute yours with a pull request.
Pack installed from the gallery — its template is on the home screen
The entry\'s pack failed validation — try updating the gallery
The gallery is empty — pull down with Refresh once you are online.
The gallery index was not found — the repository may not be published yet.
Couldn\'t reach the gallery — check the connection and refresh.
Prepare a Debian build environment (JDK 17 + Android SDK inside proot), then build and install a debug APK of this project. Experimental: first preparation downloads about 600 MB.
The build log will appear here.
Context compacted: older turns were summarised to save tokens; the agent continues from the brief.
Agent stopped: it repeated the same tools without progress. Rephrase the request or edit manually.
After each applied batch, a second model reviews the diff and the agent fixes its notes automatically
Blank = the coder model. A cheaper, faster model works well for review.
Summarise old turns when the context grows, instead of silently losing the far end
Run planning, review and context compaction on the cheapest capable model — the coder keeps yours. Only routes when the price table proves it saves, and the saved number is shown in Usage & budget
Kotlin + Jetpack Compose, Arabic/RTL — builds on the phone
The planner outlined a plan with %1$s tasks — the agent follows it below.
In team mode, this model turns each request into a task plan before coding. Blank = the coder model; a cheap fast model is ideal.
Run lint and the project tests after each batch and give the output to the reviewer
Tools of the server appear to the agent as mcp_… tools. Streamable HTTP (also works with most SSE servers).
Server added — its tools connect at the start of the next turn.
No recent crashes in the log.
WebView + zero dependencies — the fastest build on weak phones
Builds dist/app-release.apk signed with your keystore (AGP signs v1+v2+v3; release is built without shrinking to fit the phone). Passwords stay in memory and are never saved.
Keystore not found at %1$s — copy the file into the project first
Where the arm64 aapt2 comes from. Auto looks up the latest release; presets are verified community builds; a direct URL always works. The binary is ELF-verified before use.
Sign in with a device code
No token pasting: register an OAuth App once (enable Device Flow), paste its public Client ID here, then approve the request in the browser. Works on phones where copying long tokens is painful.
If the file was not touched after the build, do not install it — rebuild instead.
After a successful build, delete previous APKs in dist/ and the build intermediates to reclaim storage. The next build re-compiles from scratch.
Link any HTTPS Git host with a token — GitLab.com, Codeberg, self-hosted Gitea or Forgejo. Publishing and MRs work like on GitHub.
API type (how Saqr talks to this host)
Tokens are stored encrypted. GitLab token needs api scope; Gitea needs repo scope.
Hidden from the agent — it will never see or call this tool.
The free plan has limits (3 projects, 1 MCP server, 1 git host, no signed release builds). Pro lifts them and unlocks team agents.
3 projects · 1 MCP server · 1 git host · team agents off
Unlimited projects and MCP servers, 8 git hosts, team agents (planner + reviewer), signed release builds.
Everything in Pro at a student price — honors-system: use it only if you are studying.
Pay once, keep every Pro feature forever — including future ones.
Google Play is unavailable on this device — use the Moyasar payment link or a license token below.

Done — the plan is active. Thank you for supporting Saqr Code!

Student plan: an academic email in the license helps us honor the discount.
The free plan keeps 3 projects. Upgrade to Pro for unlimited projects and team agents.
Plan: %1$s — tap to manage or upgrade.

For the developer only: your Moyasar secret key stays in the encrypted store on this device. Create an invoice per plan, open the hosted page (mada / Apple Pay / STC Pay), then mint a license token once it is paid.

Five small steps, in order, from a fresh install to your first APK built on this device. Each completes by itself when the real thing happens.
Settings → Providers → paste your API key. Free options like Google AI Studio work.
Pick a ready template from the home screen — a landing page, a Python script, or a Compose app.
Open the project and write what you want in Arabic — copy an example below to start.
Project → Build tab → prepare the environment once, then build. Even a failed attempt teaches the path.
When the APK is built and signed this completes itself — watch the Build tab output.
Ready examples — copy one and paste it into the project chat
The path is complete — from here, describe what you want and Saqr builds it.
For servers that require OAuth. Saqr discovers the endpoints automatically — paste the client id the server issued you, then tap connect; the browser opens and lands back here.
Could not discover the OAuth endpoints — paste them manually and try again
Opening the browser to sign in…

Signed in — the server is connected

The build runs on GitHub Actions inside your own repository — your token, your repo, no Saqr cloud. Made for weak phones and low battery; the APK lands back here for one-tap install.
Connect the project to a GitHub repository from the Git tab first.
Sign in to GitHub from Settings → Accounts first.
Build workflow installed in your repository

Your settings, themes, custom commands and skill packs — encrypted on this device and backed up to a private repository you own, or shared as a file. No Saqr server, ever. A second device: link the same GitHub account, type the same passphrase, pull, apply.
Inside the snapshot: settings, themes, custom commands, skill packs, price rows, MCP server URLs — never API keys, tokens or auth headers.
Encrypts the snapshot here (AES-GCM, PBKDF2) — never stored or sent; the same phrase opens it on the other device.
owner/repo — or just a name (saqr-sync) on your account
Applying replaces the current themes, commands and packs with the snapshot\'s.
Create the private repository, then push

Run consecutive read-only tools (read, list, search, web) side by side — up to 3 at once, each with its own timeout. Results keep their order
Terminal commands such as rm -r, piping a download into a shell, writes outside /workspace or git push from the shell wait for your approval. The agent can never approve itself
Besides exact repeats, catch going in circles, the same failing call over and over, and long streaks of failed steps — nudge once, then stop
Team mode: when a task changed files, run lint and the project\'s tests before it may finish. Failures go back to the coder (up to 2 rounds) and the result is reported honestly
Retry a busy or failed model call (429, 5xx, timeout, network) once after a short pause
If the model still fails, run that step on another provider you already set up. Only providers with a saved key are offered
Keep each task\'s goal, plan, step, spend and status in .saqr/tasks so a resumed task continues where it stopped
Record every tool call (risk, decision, result, duration) in .saqr/audit.jsonl — secrets redacted, rotated at 1 MB
Web pages, search results and MCP output reach the model wrapped as data, never as instructions
Cost per task in USD (0 = off)

Checks failed — the agent is fixing them before finishing.
Stopped: the task reached its time limit. Send a message to continue.
Stopped: the task reached its cost limit. Send a message to continue.

The Chief reads each request and staffs it with the fewest roles that can do it: a question gets no team, a small edit Developer + Reviewer, a bug Debugger + Tester + Reviewer. Off = the classic Planner → Coder → Reviewer team
Let two independent read-only roles (research, reviews) run side by side. Off = one role at a time, gentler on low-memory phones
Show a rough estimate (plan size × each role\'s model price) before the team starts. Models without a price are reported, not guessed
Roles the Chief may use. The Chief and the Developer are always on; a switched-off Debugger is replaced by the Developer.
Classifies the request and runs the team
Splits large work into ordered steps with roles
Read-only: docs, versions and errors from the web
Read-only: designs the solution before coding
Finds root causes; takes over tasks that failed twice
Reviews changes for secrets, injection, auth and network risks
Runs and adds tests; no production code changes
Builds, commits and publishes when asked (push always asks you)
The Chief: a question — answered directly, no team.
Estimated cost before start: about %1$s (rough: plan size × role price)
Cost estimate unavailable: a role\'s model has no price. Add one in Usage & budget.
The planner\'s plan was unusable (a cycle or no work step) — the Chief\'s default plan runs instead.
Stopped: today\'s spend cap is reached. Raise it in Settings → Memory engine & router, or continue tomorrow.
Stopped: this month\'s spend cap is reached. Raise it in Settings → Memory engine & router.
Inject only the memories that match the request (on-device BM25, Arabic-aware) instead of the whole bank. Your preferences always ride along.
In long chats, fold old turns into a summary saved with the session and send it instead of the full history.
When a run turns failing checks green, remember the error and its fix; show matching lessons to the Debugger next time.
Keep your personal preferences across all projects (on this phone only). Only what you ask to save globally; project memory never goes there.

Pick the model per step by capability, cost and context: cheap for planning, strong for coding, an independent reviewer, a vision model for images, and failover to another configured provider. Only providers you added a key for. Off = Falcon Router as before.
Spend caps stop a run cleanly when today\'s or this month\'s priced spend reaches them (0 = off).
A summary of this chat\'s older turns, sent to the model instead of them (Rolling session summary).
No summary yet — it appears when a chat grows long and the setting is on.
Global memory is off. Nothing new is saved here; turn it on in Settings → Memory engine & router.
Name an enabled skill in a message as $skill-id (for example $ar-code-review) and it joins that run as guidance. Skills never add tools or skip approvals.
Before a run, the most relevant enabled skills are attached by on-device search (BM25). Every attachment and its reason goes to the audit log.
